On Wed, Sep 16, 2026 at 8:29 AM, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai> wrote:

Samir / Aisha,

I ran a short probe using the profile you referenced (thanks for the CSV). Notes and a compact model below. Attachment: boreal_peak_profile.xlsx (workbook with the probe results and the math).

Assumptions used in the probe:
- Model: rw-open-7b-v2 (customer-compatible); test runs for int8 and int4 quantized variants.
- Context length: avg 160 tokens (prompt + expected response buffer).
- Typical effective token generation per request: 120 tokens.
- Measured tail effects with 4x concurrent chat turns (KV-cache reuse): cache hit reduces per-request compute by ~28–45% depending on prompt reuse.

Probe results (representative):
- int8 (A100 class baseline): 1 GPU -> 2,400–2,700 tokens/sec under steady batching at moderate concurrency; p95 latency ~980ms for 120-token output when batching is enabled but with low queuing (batch windows ~30–40ms).
- int4 quantized: 1 GPU -> 3,100–3,400 tokens/sec under same conditions; p95 latency ~820–900ms.
- With aggressive KV-cache reuse observed in your profile, effective tokens/sec improves by ~25–35% because repeated prefix tokens are served from cache (so 3,100 tok/s -> ~3,875 tok/s effective on int4).

Mapping to requests/sec (RPS) for your average 120-token responses:
- int8 steady: 2,550 tok/s / 120 tok ≈ 21 RPS per GPU.
- int4 steady: 3,250 tok/s / 120 tok ≈ 27 RPS per GPU.
- With KV-cache: int4 effective ≈ 3,875 tok/s / 120 ≈ 32 RPS per GPU.

Sizing math for your observed peak concurrency (~380 concurrent):
- If your peak concurrency translates to ~380 active requests with median response time ~1.0s, steady RPS at peak ≈ 380 req/s.
- GPUs required (baseline, no headroom): 380 / 27 ≈ 14 GPUs (int4, no cache); with cache it's 380 / 32 ≈ 12 GPUs.

Recommended deployment and headroom:
- Baseline commit: 12 GPUs (int4, tuned). This covers normal peaks assuming KV-cache effectiveness as observed.
- Burst buffer: +4 GPUs dedicated to handle short high-concurrency spikes and model warmup. This yields effective headroom of ~33%.
- Conservative option: 16 GPUs committed if you prefer fewer autoscale operations and more predictable latency at p99.

Notes on latency / SLO fit:
- For p95 <= 1.2s target, int4 with cache and headroom above is a good fit.
- p99 behavior depends on queueing during simultaneous large bursts; recommend a short (100–300ms) request shedding / graceful degraded-response policy for extreme spikes, and fallback model variant for very large requests.

Operational suggestions:
- Set KV-cache TTLs to 30–60s for chat sessions to maximize reuse without growing memory unbounded.
- Observe prefix-reuse ratio in first 2 weeks post-rollout; if reuse <15%, revisit batch/window settings (we can help tune).

I'll attach the probe workbook and a one-pager SLO mapping. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the spreadsheet.

— Priyom

Samir / Procurement team — attaching the recommended sizing + SLO mapping PDF (slo_mapping.pdf) and the probe workbook (boreal_peak_profile.xlsx). Summary of our recommendation:

- Recommended initial commit: 12 GPUs (int4 quantized profile) in a Dedicated pool.
- Burst/Autoscale headroom: 4 additional GPUs to handle short peaks (recommended policy: automatic burst up to +4 for windows <= 10 minutes).
- Expected steady p95 latency: ~0.82–0.95s (meets your 1.2s p95 target).
- Expected p99: ~1.6–2.1s under recommended headroom; if you want p99 < 1.5s we recommend moving to 16 GPUs committed.
- KV-cache: recommended TTL 45s; expect effective RPS gains of 20–35% depending on reuse.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm procurement timeline and whether you want the conservative 16-GPU commit or 12+burst.
2) If you confirm 12+burst, we'll provision a short 2-week canary window to validate real-world prefix reuse and adjust batch windows.
3) We'll provide a tailored pricing estimate and a simple runbook for warmup and autoscale triggers.

Happy to run a 30-minute walkthrough with your infra/procurement folks if helpful.

Regards,
